Online Indian Singing Classes

From Sa Re Ga Ma to ragas and bhajans: build pitch, breath and confidence.

Live one-to-one Indian singing lessons on Zoom or Google Meet with Vini Devda, rooted in Hindustani classical training. Ideal if you believe you cannot sing, and just as useful for experienced singers who want raga, bhajan and kirtan technique. Each online class lasts 40 minutes; a single class costs ₹1,500 (≈ US$17) and 10 classes cost ₹13,500 (≈ US$153).

Who this class is for

  • "I can't sing" beginners — we start from your natural voice
  • Yoga teachers and kirtan leaders who want a steadier, stronger voice
  • Singers from other styles (pop, jazz, choir) exploring Indian music
  • Spiritual seekers who want to chant mantras correctly

What you will be able to do

  • Find your natural Sa and sing in tune with a tanpura drone
  • Breathe from the diaphragm and sing without strain
  • Practise alankars and paltas that build accuracy and agility
  • Understand what a raga is and sing Raga Bhupali and Raga Yaman
  • Sing 3–5 bhajans and kirtans with meaning and feeling (bhava)
  • Keep time in Teentaal and Keharwa while you sing

What you learn, class by class

Foundation: classes 1–5

  1. The Indian swaras. Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa with a tanpura drone; natural (shuddh), flat (komal) and sharp (tivra) notes; the three octaves; holding a steady Sa.
  2. Voice culture and breath. Diaphragmatic breathing, pranayama for singers (anulom vilom, bhastrika), warm-ups that protect the voice, and posture.
  3. Alankars and paltas. The classic patterns that train accuracy and flexibility, and a 15–20 minute daily routine.
  4. What a raga is. Note selection, mood and time of day, the most important notes (vadi and samvadi), and your first raga, Bhupali.
  5. Your first bhajan. Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram or Om Namah Shivaya, with its meaning, melody, rhythm and feeling (bhava).

Intermediate: classes 6–10

  1. Raga Yaman. Its structure, slow alaap, simple taans and a short bandish (composition).
  2. Tala for singers. Teentaal (16 beats) and Keharwa (8 beats), and singing a bhajan while clapping the tala.
  3. Kirtan technique. Call and response, building intensity, repeating a phrase without strain, and basic harmonium accompaniment.
  4. Mantra chanting. Sanskrit pronunciation and breath-aligned chanting: Gayatri Mantra, Mahamrityunjaya Mantra and Om Namah Shivaya.
  5. Performance. Prepare two or three pieces, record yourself, and leave with a personal plan for what to learn next.

How a 40-minute online class runs

  • Warm-up and breathing exercises to prepare your voice safely.
  • Core teaching: raga, alankar or bhajan, depending on your level and goals.
  • Practice together with personal feedback, then homework for the week.
  • Afterwards: the recording of the class and any notation or lyrics as a PDF.

What you need

  • Just your voice — no instrument is needed to start
  • A laptop or tablet with Zoom or Google Meet, a stable connection and headphones
  • A quiet space where you can sing freely

Founder and lead teacher

Vini Devda

Vini Devda is the third generation of a family of musicians and began learning Indian classical music at the age of five in the traditional guru–shishya way. Vini Devda holds a degree in Indian Classical Vocal Music from Government College, Ajmer, has taught students from 25+ countries since 2008, and leads the Chokhi Vini Project, the school's Rajasthani folk band.

I believe everyone is musical — the question is not 'Can I learn?' but 'Am I ready to open my ears and heart?' I've taught complete beginners who thought they were tone-deaf, and watched them lead kirtans 10 weeks later. Music is patience, practice, and playfulness.

  • Teaching since 2008 (18+ years)
  • Degree in Indian Classical Vocal Music, Government College, Ajmer
  • Teaches: Tabla, Hindustani classical vocal, Harmonium, Sitar, Dholak
  • Leads the Chokhi Vini Project folk band

Frequently asked questions

How much do online classes cost?

A single online class starts at ₹1,500, and packages bring the price down to ₹1,300 per class. Every class page shows its prices in Indian rupees with an approximate conversion to US dollars, euros or pounds.

How do I pay?

UPI or bank transfer (India), PayPal or Wise (international). Prices are set in Indian rupees; if you pay from abroad, PayPal or Wise converts the amount.

What if I do not enjoy my first class?

Not happy after your first class? We refund it in full.

Can I reschedule a class?

Reschedule free of charge up to 4 hours before your class.

How long are packages valid?

5-class packages are valid for 3 months and 10-class packages for 6 months. Unused classes can be gifted to a friend or family member.

I think I am tone-deaf. Can I still learn?

Yes. Pitch is a skill that can be trained: we start with one steady note (Sa) against a drone and build from there. Many students arrive convinced they cannot sing.

Is this Hindustani or Carnatic singing?

Hindustani (North Indian) classical singing, together with devotional bhajan and kirtan. We do not teach Carnatic (South Indian) music.

Do I need to read music?

No. Indian music is taught by ear. We use sargam (Sa Re Ga Ma) and lyric sheets with transliteration.
